sn41.1:2.3: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’: do these things differ in both meaning and phrasing? Or do they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing?”
sn41.1:2.4: Some senior mendicants answered like this:
sn41.1:2.5: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’: these things differ in both meaning and phrasing.”
sn41.1:2.6: But some senior mendicants answered like this:
sn41.1:2.7: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’ mean the same thing; they differ only in the phrasing.”

sn41.1:4.13: Nor is the nose the fetter of smells …
sn41.1:4.14: Nor is the tongue the fetter of tastes …
sn41.1:4.15: Nor is the body the fetter of touches, nor are touches the fetter of the body;
sn41.1:4.16: The fetter there is the desire and greed that arises from the pair of them.
